name: CSS
note: Not styling. In this yard CSS is the computer: counters do the arithmetic, :has() is the state, and the cascade settles what is true. A hundred and forty boards decide things in a stylesheet with no script anywhere.
ground: Three facts the boards are built on. A counter prints only after whatever increments it, so order of appearance is order of evaluation. An element with display:none generates no box and so increments nothing, which is how you branch. And cascade order settles only ties — origin, then layer, then specificity, then source order — so a rule that loses is not a rule that ran and failed, it is a rule that never applied.
ask: Where is the state kept, and what would you have to press to change it?
